From eaa2f87c6b840b83827c40db6eb8481689570259 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Aug 2017 13:30:30 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] x86/ldt: Fix off by one in get_segment_base()

ldt->entries[] is allocated in alloc_ldt_struct().  It has
ldt->nr_entries elements and ldt->nr_entries is capped at LDT_ENTRIES.
So if "idx" is == ldt->nr_entries then we're reading beyond the end of
the buffer.  It seems duplicative to have two limit checks when one
would work just as well so I removed the check against LDT_ENTRIES.

The gdt_page.gdt[] array has GDT_ENTRIES entries.

Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Acked-by: Andy Lutomirski <luto@kernel.org>
Cc: Alexander Shishkin <alexander.shishkin@linux.intel.com>
Cc: Arnaldo Carvalho de Melo <acme@kernel.org>
Cc: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Cc: Peter Zijlstra <peterz@infradead.org>
Cc: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Cc: kernel-janitors@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: d07bdfd322d3 ("perf/x86: Fix USER/KERNEL tagging of samples properly")
Link: http://lkml.kernel.org/r/20170818102516.gqwm4xdvvuvjw5ho@mwanda
Signed-off-by: Ingo Molnar <mingo@kernel.org>

diff --git a/arch/x86/events/core.c b/arch/x86/events/core.c
index af12e294caed..939050169d12 100644
--- a/arch/x86/events/core.c
+++ b/arch/x86/events/core.c
@@ -2335,12 +2335,9 @@ static unsigned long get_segment_base(unsigned int segment)
 #ifdef CONFIG_MODIFY_LDT_SYSCALL
 		struct ldt_struct *ldt;
 
-		if (idx > LDT_ENTRIES)
-			return 0;
-
 		/* IRQs are off, so this synchronizes with smp_store_release */
 		ldt = lockless_dereference(current->active_mm->context.ldt);
-		if (!ldt || idx > ldt->nr_entries)
+		if (!ldt || idx >= ldt->nr_entries)
 			return 0;
 
 		desc = &ldt->entries[idx];
@@ -2348,7 +2345,7 @@ static unsigned long get_segment_base(unsigned int segment)
 		return 0;
 #endif
 	} else {
-		if (idx > GDT_ENTRIES)
+		if (idx >= GDT_ENTRIES)
 			return 0;
 
 		desc = raw_cpu_ptr(gdt_page.gdt) + idx;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/x86/events/core.c`**
   - Removed the check `if (idx > LDT_ENTRIES)` which was redundant since `idx` should not exceed the number of entries in the LDT.
   - Changed the condition `if (!ldt || idx > ldt->nr_entries)` to `if (!ldt || idx >= ldt->nr_entries)` to prevent reading beyond the allocated entries in the LDT.
   - Similarly, modified the condition `if (idx > GDT_ENTRIES)` to `if (idx >= GDT_ENTRIES)` to ensure that the index does not exceed the number of entries in the GDT.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in the `arch/x86/events/core.c` file are related to improving the boundary checks for accessing the LDT and GDT structures. The changes ensure that the index `idx` is checked against the number of entries in both the LDT and GDT correctly, preventing potential out-of-bounds access. By consolidating the checks and ensuring they are inclusive (`>=`), the patch enhances the safety and correctness of the segment base retrieval function, addressing a bug that could lead to reading beyond allocated memory.

Here is the commit message:
x86/ldt: Fix off by one in get_segment_base()

ldt->entries[] is allocated in alloc_ldt_struct().  It has
ldt->nr_entries elements and ldt->nr_entries is capped at LDT_ENTRIES.
So if "idx" is == ldt->nr_entries then we're reading beyond the end of
the buffer.  It seems duplicative to have two limit checks when one
would work just as well so I removed the check against LDT_ENTRIES.

The gdt_page.gdt[] array has GDT_ENTRIES entries.

Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Acked-by: Andy Lutomirski <luto@kernel.org>
Cc: Alexander Shishkin <alexander.shishkin@linux.intel.com>
Cc: Arnaldo Carvalho de Melo <acme@kernel.org>
Cc: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Cc: Peter Zijlstra <peterz@infradead.org>
Cc: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Cc: kernel-janitors@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: d07bdfd322d3 ("perf/x86: Fix USER/KERNEL tagging of samples properly")
Link: http://lkml.kernel.org/r/20170818102516.gqwm4xdvvuvjw5ho@mwanda
Signed-off-by: Ingo Molnar <mingo@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by an off-by-one error in the boundary checks for accessing the entries in the LDT (Local Descriptor Table) and GDT (Global Descriptor Table). The original checks allowed for the possibility of accessing an index equal to the number of entries, which is out of bounds since valid indices range from 0 to `nr_entries - 1`. This could lead to reading invalid memory and potential system instability or crashes.

Here is the patch:
 
 static unsigned long get_segment_base(unsigned int segment)
 {
 	struct desc_struct *desc;
 	unsigned int idx = segment >> 3;
 
 	if ((segment & SEGMENT_TI_MASK) == SEGMENT_LDT) {
 #ifdef CONFIG_MODIFY_LDT_SYSCALL
 		struct ldt_struct *ldt;
 
-		if (idx > LDT_ENTRIES)
-			return 0;
-
 		/* IRQs are off, so this synchronizes with smp_store_release */
 		ldt = lockless_dereference(current->active_mm->context.ldt);
-		if (!ldt || idx > ldt->nr_entries)
+		if (!ldt || idx >= ldt->nr_entries)
 			return 0;
 
 		desc = &ldt->entries[idx];
 #else
 		return 0;
 #endif
 	} else {
-		if (idx > GDT_ENTRIES)
+		if (idx >= GDT_ENTRIES)
 			return 0;
 
 		desc = raw_cpu_ptr(gdt_page.gdt) + idx;
 	}
 
 	return get_desc_base(desc);
 }

```

```
```c

```
Reason:
The bug occurs due to off-by-one errors in the boundary checks for accessing the entries in the LDT and GDT. The condition `idx > ldt->nr_entries` and `idx > GDT_ENTRIES` allow for the possibility of accessing an index equal to the number of entries, which is out of bounds since valid indices range from 0 to `nr_entries - 1`. This can lead to reading invalid memory, causing potential system instability or crashes.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (idx >= ldt->nr_entries)
```
```c
if (idx >= GDT_ENTRIES)
```
Reason:
The fix changes the boundary checks from `>` to `>=`, ensuring that the index `idx` cannot equal the number of entries, thus preventing out-of-bounds access. This ensures that valid indices remain within the range of 0 to `nr_entries - 1` for LDT and 0 to `GDT_ENTRIES - 1` for GDT, thereby eliminating the risk of reading invalid memory.
